content: The UC Davis School of Medicine was established in 1966 and graduated its first class of physicians in 1972. The school operates research facilities on the Davis campus, while the majority of its teaching and clinical activities are conducted in Sacramento, located 17 miles east of the Davis campus. In December 2006, the school opened a new Education Building, marking the transition of all medical school classes to the Sacramento campus. Research activities are expected to continue at both campuses for the foreseeable future. Due to its small class size, desirable location in Northern California, and relatively affordable tuition, admission to the UC Davis School of Medicine is highly competitive. In 2005, the school received 4,109 applications, offered interviews to 392 applicants, and matriculated 93 students, resulting in an acceptance rate of approximately 6 percent. In 2007, the school was ranked 30 in primary care methodology and 49 in research methodology by U.S. News & World Report. The UC Davis Medical Center, located in Sacramento, is one of five teaching hospitals within the University of California system. Other affiliated hospitals include the UC Davis Children’s Hospital, the UC Davis Cancer Center, Shriners Hospitals for Children Northern California, and the Sacramento VA Medical Center. The faculty at the UC Davis School of Medicine engage in a broad spectrum of basic and applied research, including neuroscience, cancer biology, vascular biology, genetic diseases, functional genomics, health services, infectious diseases, nutrition, telemedicine, and vision science. The school receives approximately $90 million annually in funding from the National Institutes of Health (NIH). About half of the medical students at UC Davis participate in research during their training. The UC Davis School of Medicine is renowned for its student-run clinics, which provide free primary care services to uninsured, low-income, and underserved populations in Sacramento and surrounding areas. These clinics not only deliver high-quality healthcare to patients but also offer medical students valuable real-world clinical experience early in their training.
